title: Linear Equation Preserved Each Algebra Move
text: id: COMP-010 domain: math title: Linear Equation Preserved Each Algebra Move tags: algebra, equation, solve memory: An equation once went wrong when I skipped from the original line to the answer. I slowed down and preserved each move: expand, combine like terms, move constants, divide. Each line had to still equal the previous line. The final x survived substitution because no step disappeared.

title: Money Problems Kept Cents To Two Decimal Places
text: id: COMP-019 domain: math title: Money Problems Kept Cents To Two Decimal Places tags: money, rounding, decimals memory: A money answer once looked close but failed because I rounded too early. I kept cents through the calculation and rounded only at the final bill. The tax, fee, credit, and tier amounts each got two decimal places. The final dollar amount became both readable and exact enough.

title: Ratio Mixture Counted Total Parts Before Liters
text: id: COMP-009 domain: math title: Ratio Mixture Counted Total Parts Before Liters tags: ratio, mixture, parts memory: A mixture ratio felt like two numbers competing until I counted total parts. Two parts and five parts made seven equal chunks of the final volume. I found liters per part first, then multiplied by each side of the ratio. The concentrate and water added back to the requested total.

title: Fractions Simplified After The Correct Multiplication
text: id: COMP-020 domain: math title: Fractions Simplified After The Correct Multiplication tags: fractions, probability, simplify memory: A probability fraction once simplified beautifully from the wrong multiplication. I learned to get the event structure correct before reducing anything. First the changed counts, then multiplication, then simplification, then an optional decimal. A neat fraction is only useful after the setup is true.

title: Ticket Table Solved Each Team Before Comparing
text: id: COMP-011 domain: math title: Ticket Table Solved Each Team Before Comparing tags: table, comparison, tickets memory: A support dashboard question once fooled me because I compared teams before finishing their individual ledgers. I gave Team A its own start, closed, received calculation, then did the same for Team B. Only then did I total and compare. The table made the winner obvious.
